purpose: Clarithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including chest infections, throat infections, skin infections, and sinus infections. It is also used as part of a combination treatment to get rid of H. pylori, a stomach bacteria that can cause ulcers. Your doctor prescribes it specifically because it works well against the type of bacteria causing your infection.
how_it_works: Clarithromycin works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply — without those proteins, they cannot survive or spread. Over time, your immune system is then able to clear the remaining bacteria from your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related, including nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, and an upset stomach. You may also notice an unusual or metallic taste in your mouth while taking it. These effects are usually mild and get better as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, liver disease, or kidney disease, as this medication may not be safe for you in those situations. Clarithromycin can interact with many other medications, including some cholesterol drugs, blood thinners, and heart medicines, so always share your full medication list with your pharmacist. Stop taking it and contact your doctor right away if you develop a severe rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, irregular heartbeat, or severe diarrhea.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken twice a day, roughly every 12 hours. The extended-release tablet (Biaxin XL) is typically taken once a day with food. Always finish the full course of antibiotics your doctor prescribed, even if you start feeling better early, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
